summary: This diff adds a new file, report.md, an Adversarial Review 2 report critiquing a follow-the-sun on-call rotation plan (Krakow/US-East). It concludes the plan fails from day one: a 6-hour nightly coverage hole caused by undefined "closest" routing, and an all-US incident-commander pool that forces overnight US pages, undermining the plan's own success metric. It ranks ten findings (two Critical, three High, four Medium, one Low), proposes four minimum fixes (UTC-based schedule tiling, IC reconciliation, deeper escalation, and a verified go-live readiness gate), and includes a summary table, per-finding failure scenarios and root causes, a killed-findings section (none killed), open verification items, and yes/no retest criteria.

claims.text: The plan leaves a 6-hour nightly coverage hole (01:00-07:00 UTC / 20:00-02:00 ET) with routing left to an undefined "closest" rule.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: 6-hour nightly coverage hole with undefined "closest" routing (F1)

claims.text: The incident-commander pool is entirely US-based with no IC paging schedule defined, so a Sev1 inside Krakow's window still requires waking a US engineer.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: All-US IC pool forces overnight US pages for every Krakow-window Sev1 (F2)

claims.text: The escalation chain defines exactly one hop, which by construction lands on an off-shift (asleep) engineer, then dead-ends with no further tier.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: Escalation chain is one hop into a sleeping engineer, then dead-ends (F4)

claims.text: The 3-person, 12-hour Krakow rotation collapses on the first absence, degrading into a page-forwarding delay in front of the old US overnight rotation.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: 3-person, 12-hour rotation collapses on the first absence (F5)

claims.text: Go-live is gated by a calendar date while Krakow's prod access provisioning is still "in progress," with severity rated Plausible pending verification of the actual provisioning completion date.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: Go-live is calendar-gated while Krakow prod access is incomplete (F3)

claims.text: The single success metric (zero overnight PagerDuty pages) can go green while incidents are displaced into escalations, calls, IC activations, or suppressed/downgraded alerts.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: Success metric can go green while every real failure mode worsens (F6)

claims.text: All twelve adversary findings survived verification and merged into seven; none were killed.
Polish statutory minimum leave exceeds 20 days, used to justify the two-week absence scenario.
claims.anchor: ### Finding: 3-person, 12-hour rotation collapses on the first absence (F5)
